title: Congenital Heart Adhesion Prevention (CHAP) Study
summary:
Congenital heart defects are the most common congenital malformations that result in multiple surgeries beginning at birth. Each of these heart surgeries results in local adhesions between vascular, cardiac and bony structures. During follow-up cardiac surgery, these adhesions pose some risk because life-threatening bleeding can occur during reopening of the sternum and freeing of the structures on the heart. To reduce the risk of subsequent surgery and prevent adhesions from forming (adhesion prophylaxis), medical device manufacturers provide agents for local application to the heart. These agents are applied to the cardiac structures at the end of surgery before closure of the sternum.
This study will compare two different available medical devices (Coseal® and 4Dry-Field® PH) and isotonic saline. "Isotonic" simply means that the saline solution has the same salt concentration as human blood. The medical devices (Coseal® and 4DryField® PH) are approved for pediatric cardiac surgery and are routinely used there, as is isotonic saline. In the neonatal and infant age, the first operation is usually performed to secure the natural blood flow from the heart into the systemic circulation and to create an artificial connection to the pulmonary circulation (application of a so-called shunt). Adhesion prophylaxis is applied to the heart before closure of the sternum. Which of the three adhesion prophylaxis products is applied is determined randomly. In order to objectively verify the correct application of adhesion prophylaxis, the procedure is video-recorded. Within the first year of life, the applied shunt is removed again during the subsequent surgery. The second operation is also part of the standard treatment. During this second operation, it is assessed whether the goal of reducing or avoiding adhesions has been achieved. The evaluation is done by independent examiners. Since the examiners are not present during the operation, the operation is video-recorded and the evaluation is based on the visual material.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Newborns and infants (within 90 days after birth) with congenital cardiac anomaly who receive a systemic-to-pulmonary shunt via sternotomy. Shunt procedure (OP1) can be performed with or without CPB and include: Blalock-Taussig shunt, central aorto-pulmonary shunt and xano-shunt (right ventricular to pulmonary artery shunt).
2. The patient’s legal representative(s) approve(s) the patient’s participation in the study by signing the informed consent.
3. Anticipation that the second sternotomy procedure (OP2: bidirectional Glenn, corrective surgery or shunt-exchange) will be performed at an age of the patient beyond 2 months and within the first year of life.
4. Anticipation that both OP1 and OP2 are performed in a study center.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Previous sternotomy except for bilateral pulmonary artery banding procedure
2. Shock (mechanical circulatory support and/or lactate > 5 mmol/l within 48 hours before surgery)
3. Infection (CRP > 20 mg/l within 48 hours before surgery)
4. Kidney failure (serum creatinine > 1.5 mg/dl or urine output < 0.5 ml/kg/h within 48 hours before surgery)
5. Known intolerance to starchy or polyethylene glycol - containing substances
6. The patient is participating in another device or drug study
